name: Asset Import & Setup
description: Scans a folder for assets, detects types, applies matching presets, and generates a change summary.
toolGroupNotes: Every tool in this workflow (manage_asset, batch_execute, read_console) is in the bridge's default-on `core` group, so no manage_tools activation step is needed. IMPORTANT on the scan step: manage_asset's search_pattern is Unity's AssetDatabase filter syntax, NOT a filename glob (verified on bridge 10.3.0, 2026-10-21). `*` returns everything under path; `t:MonoScript` / `t:Texture2D` / `t:Shader` / `t:Model` filter by type; a bare name substring matches on name. An `*.ext` pattern such as `*.fbx` matches NOTHING and still returns success:true with zero assets, which makes the whole workflow a silent no-op that reports `0 succeeded`. Narrow this step with a `t:` filter, never with a glob, and if a scan returns zero assets re-run it with `*` before reporting the folder empty. See steering/asset-automation.md. Keep batch_execute to Unity-side work like this: the batch path bypasses the Python server layer, so a server-layer action (verified: manage_editor telemetry_status/telemetry_ping) fails inside a batch with a misleading `Unknown action` error -- retest any such failure as a direct call before concluding the action does not exist. On Unity 6.4, note that a dependent asset reimports only when its dependency's import result changes -- a project with custom ScriptedImporter/AssetPostprocessor code may need explicit DependsOnSourceAsset/DependsOnArtifact declarations for a batch apply to propagate (source: https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.6/manual/upgrade-guides/upgrade-guide-unity64, retrieved 2026-10-21). See steering/asset-automation.md.

steps.name: Scan asset folder (search_pattern is an AssetDatabase filter, not a filename glob)
Detect asset types by naming patterns (per matched asset)
Apply matching presets via batch execute (fail_fast must be false so one bad asset does not abandon the rest)
